_nota: Conservative, informational FOLLOW-UP guidance. Not diagnoses or prescriptions. Every Act alert includes notifying the Medical Officer and following the authorized mission protocols. Combined rules are evaluated first. Keys and level identifiers (amarillo = Watch, rojo = Act) are internal and not translated.

combinadas.titulo: Physiological stress pattern (resting HR ↑ and variability ↓)
combinadas.mensaje: Resting heart rate rose and heart rate variability fell at the same time, compared with what is usual for this person. Wearable studies have seen this pattern before infection symptoms, but it also appears with stress, poor recovery or exercise load. It is not a diagnosis.
acciones: Log symptoms (temperature, malaise, skin) in the check-in
Reduce today's exercise intensity if the mission plan allows
Repeat the measurement in 24 h

combinadas.titulo: Fatigue: shorter sleep and more attention lapses
combinadas.mensaje: Slept less than usual and lapses increased on the psychomotor vigilance test (PVT-B). Sleep loss reduces PVT performance.
acciones: Consider postponing critical tasks that need sustained attention
Prioritize tonight's rest period
Repeat the PVT-B tomorrow

combinadas.titulo: Behavioral change: lower mood and worse cognitive performance
combinadas.mensaje: Self-reported mood and the vigilance test worsened at the same time compared with what is usual. The 520-day Mars-500 analog mission showed very different behavioral and sleep changes between crew members.
acciones: Follow-up conversation with the Medical Officer or a trusted crewmate
Keep exercise, sleep and (delayed) family contact routines
Repeat check-in and PVT-B tomorrow
Hydrate and rest; avoid comparing with other crew members
Repeat the measurement in 24 h

rojo.titulo: Resting heart rate well above usual
acciones: Log symptoms in the check-in
Limit physical effort until the medical review

amarillo.titulo: Heart rate variability lower than usual
acciones: Prioritize recovery: sleep and breaks
Repeat the measurement tomorrow

rojo.titulo: Heart rate variability very low for this person
acciones: Review workload and exercise with the Medical Officer
Repeat the measurement tomorrow
Check schedule, light and noise during the rest period
Watch next night's sleep

rojo.titulo: Sleep much shorter than usual for this person
acciones: Consider postponing critical tasks
Arrange a rest period with the crew

amarillo.titulo: Radiation dose rate higher than usual
acciones: Check the dosimeter reading and its usual location
Check the onboard log of solar activity

rojo.titulo: Very high dose rate (possible solar particle event)
acciones: Follow the mission's solar event procedure authorized by the Commander and the Medical Officer
Record the cumulative dose in the report to Earth
Take a short break and repeat the PVT-B later
Check the previous night's sleep

rojo.titulo: Attention much lower than usual for this person
acciones: Consider postponing critical tasks that need sustained attention
Rest and repeat the PVT-B
Talk with a trusted crewmate
Keep exercise and delayed-communication routines
Follow-up conversation with the Medical Officer
Use the psychological support resources planned by the mission

escalado_rojo: Notify the onboard Medical Officer and follow the authorized mission protocols.
aviso: Rule-based follow-up guidance from a statistical detection. Not a diagnosis or a treatment instruction.
